sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sepen entry (sec. 2.23.12.12, pp. 143-144) is the first identification of the language: villages Akukum and Sepen, 'The language has not been recorded previously', lexical percentages only (Sepen-Mikarew 60%, Sepen-Giri 60%); Misegian typology (p. 145) lists phonemes only. General remark p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' — applies to all languages in the study; nothing Sepen-specific.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [accessed 2026-09-21]. Ruboni Range. In T. Usher & E. Suter (eds), New Guinea World: mapping the languages of New Guinea (Dept. of Comparative Language Science, Univ. of Zurich). Family page with proto-Ruboni Range (Misegian) reconstruction and reflex tables for Mikarew, Makarub (Capell), Sepen (Z'graggen 1972), Akukem (Daniels 2010, digitalized by R. Barlow), Giri, Kire.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No synchronic statement. Usher's only prosodic remarks are diachronic: initial consonants are 'secondary developments due to the loss of a destressed initial vowel.. /*ʉ/' (line 80) and 'Most Ruboni Range roots begin with vowels, which are then very often lost, presumably due to thematic stress' (line 1263). DATA (marks only): Daniels' Akukem forms are reproduced with IPA primary-stress marks in 139 table cells = 45 distinct glosses of 146; 39 are marked on the root-final syllable (31 disyllables, e.g. mbɨˈtɨm 'tail', rɨˈɣor 'heart', raˈku 'sleep'; 8 trisyllables, e.g. aroˈroŋ 'egg', ukuˈruk…

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John A. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C38.731
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 732 lists features 'widespread throughout the phylum, and.. found in a majority of the languages which comprise it', among them 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems', low vowel inventories and a quasi-phonemic schwa; p. 758 says the Ramu Super-Stock shows 'the Sepik-Ramu phonology.. strongly in evidence'. No statement locates word stress for any Ramu language and Sepen is never discussed individually; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in the chapter.
